extracted.intended_audience: OPQA reviewers and USPTO patent examiners (patent quality assurance personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for OPQA reviewers to evaluate the statutory compliance and overall quality of patent office actions (rejections, omissions, searches, 112(f) analysis, restriction, etc.). Used to determine whether rejections correctly identify claims/statute and are supported by sufficient evidence and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness and sufficiency of patentability determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejecting a claim, to meet the Office’s burden of establishing unpatentability, the patentability determination must be correct and must, at a minimum, (1) identify the claim and relevant statute, and (2) set forth sufficient evidence to put a person skilled in the art on notice as to why the claim is unpatentable so as to provide applicant with a fair opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiency is considered in the context of the entire prosecution history, including examiner explanations. Correctness is evaluated based on whether determinations were reasonable (not reviewer hindsight or what the reviewer would have done).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority documented
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the assigned examiner and the individual signing the Office action are the same (Examiner with Signatory Authority) or different (Examiner without Signatory Authority); if different, document whether the signature block indicates SPE or another examiner with authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless clear evidence to the contrary, assume the signer has appropriate signatory authority. Use checkboxes to mark status; special handling for unsigned actions in SPE/TC/Ad Hoc use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record rejections made checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Document which rejections were made in the Office action (None; 35 USC 102; 35 USC 103; 35 USC 112(a) enablement; 35 USC 112(a) written description; 35 USC 112(b); 35 USC 112(d); 35 USC 101 subject matter eligibility; 35 USC 101 utility; 35 USC 101 statutory double patenting; Nonstatutory double patenting; Other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check all that apply to capture the scope of rejections in the action under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted rejections checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether any rejections were omitted that should have been made (same statute list as rejections made).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to flag omitted grounds of rejection for TC consideration where appropriate; separate omitted-rejection sections exist for each statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102 rejection compliance — identify claim/statute and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 102 rejection is made, determine whether all 35 USC 102 rejection(s) in the Office action are in compliance (Yes/No). Compliance requires properly identifying the claim(s), the statute (including subparagraphs) and being supported by sufficient evidence to support anticipation of the claim(s) by the applied disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult statutory compliance scenarios for assistance in determining compliance. If compliant, proceed to accolade/characteristics questions; if noncompliant, document details in following questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims linked to noncompliant 102 rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: List each claim discussed individually as a basis for noncompliance; include dependent claims which inherit the noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an Explanation of Noncompliance section documenting reasons for each listed claim. Also indicate whether the noncompliance originates in independent claims, dependent claims, or both (select one of: only independent, only dependent, both).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for alternate compliant prior art rejection when 102 noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims with a noncompliant 102 rejection, determine whether another compliant prior art rejection (either under 102 or 103) was applied to those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every claim listed as noncompliant under 102 also has another compliant prior art rejection, answer Yes; otherwise No. If Yes, indicate whether the compliant prior art rejection was applied under 102 and/or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102 noncompliance reason — failure to properly identify claims/statute
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute/subparagraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT use this box when the reviewer concludes the reference fails to anticipate claims (that is lack of evidence — use the insufficient evidence box). Use this when the claim listing or statutory subparagraph applied is incorrect. Explain specifically how claims/statute identification is deficient; avoid rhetorical or personalized language.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102 noncompliance reason — disclosure not prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure(s) relied upon does not qualify as prior art under any subparagraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure is available as prior art but not under the subparagraph applied, select the failure to identify statute box instead. Provide an explanation as to why the disclosure is not available as prior art; keep comments factual and professional.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102 noncompliance reason — insufficient evidence to demonstrate anticipation under BRI
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not provide sufficient evidence to demonstrate that the disclosure teaches every element required by the claim under its Broadest Reasonable Interpretation (BRI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this is checked, at least one of two subboxes must be checked: (1) no citation(s)/mapping to the prior art for the missing element(s), or (2) mapping provided but the relevant portion does not provide sufficient evidence to meet the limitation(s). For each claim and limitation identified, explain how the reference fails to meet the limitation and why the applied interpretation is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: No citation/mapping for missing limitation (102)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection gives no guidance for how the limitation(s) identified as basis for noncompliance is met by the reference (no mapping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures when the rejection provides no correlation at all for the missing limitation(s). Provide examples and cite precisely which limitation lacks mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping provided but relevant portions insufficient (102)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection maps the limitation(s) to the prior art, but the relevant portion(s) do not provide sufficient evidence to meet the limitation(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which portions were mapped and why they are insufficient to support anticipation (technical/claim construction reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional noncompliance/quality flags for 102 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Check applicable issues contributing to noncompliance: (a) rejection included obviousness rationale; (b) improper reliance on features from different embodiments; (c) improper reliance on inherency; (d) non-compliance due to unreasonable claim interpretation; (e) part of a combined 102/103 rejection; (f) none of the above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each box checked, include an explanation in the corresponding comment box that supports the selection. Do not guess root causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 102 rejection comments / best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional comments providing suggestions, feedback, or best practices for the examiner that are NOT directed to the basis of a noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewer suggests a compliant prior art rejection for TC consideration, include details here. Keep suggestions constructive and separate from noncompliance write-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — claim grouping and claim lumping
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection addresses substantially all claims individually and only groups together claims that are of substantially similar scope (limited claim lumping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check this when the rejection treats claims individually where necessary and groups only similar claims; avoids overbroad lumping that hides differences between claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — reasonably pinpoints where limitations are met
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection reasonably pinpoints where substantially all limitations are met by the prior art (e.g., points to specific locations in the written specification or drawings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should be checked when the rejection points to precise locations. Do not check if the rejection refers only to large portions of the reference or generally to a figure without specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — includes pasted figures with annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection includes pasted pertinent figures with annotations (as appropriate) which pinpoint where limitations are met by the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of annotated figures usually aids clarity and should be noted; it's a characteristic of thorough rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — explains how/why limitations are met or equates terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection goes beyond pinpointing where the limitations are taught by summarizing how/why the limitations are met by the prior art or reciting terminology from the prior art to equate with terminology from the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this is checked, the 'reasonably pinpoints' characteristic should also be checked. This indicates the rejection provides explanatory analysis, not merely mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — statements of patentable weight
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection includes statements of patentable weight, particularly when patentable weight is not being given to intended use limitations, preambles, or claim language that suggests optional structure or steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note when the examiner assigns patentable weight to elements that may not warrant it; document such interpretive choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — claim interpretation stated
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection sets forth a claim interpretation that points out how the examiner is interpreting the claim/term/phrase for purposes of the rejection (e.g., BRI, special definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection explicitly states an interpretation; this helps reviewers assess reasonableness of the construction applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — 112(f) related explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For limitations invoking 112(f), the rejection explains how the prior art structure was either the same as the disclosed corresponding structure or an equivalent thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only check when the body of the art rejection expressly mentions that the reference structure is same or equivalent to the corresponding disclosed structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — inclusion of detailed legal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action included detailed legal analysis of applicable legal issues through analysis of the claims and the case law/policy that applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when the rejection contains substantiated legal reasoning and citation to relevant case law/policy, not just conclusion statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — inclusion of detailed technical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action included detailed technical analysis regarding the invention and/or the applicability of the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical rationale that shows understanding of the invention and prior art supports stronger rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of 102 rejections — includes suggestions to overcome rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office action included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejection(s) (not general 'FP' language or merely indicating claims with allowable subject matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions should be substantive and actionable rather than generic; note when included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accolade eligibility for 102 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If all 102 rejections are compliant and certain characteristics are present (per current accolade procedures), the reviewer may indicate whether an accolade is appropriate and provide the required sentence completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult current accolade procedures and guidance documents before marking Yes; discipline-specific procedures apply for completing accolade wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie case requirement for 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: To support an obviousness conclusion, the rejection should articulate a prima facie case: findings of fact supported by sufficient evidence in the prior art; articulate how the prior art is to be modified to arrive at the claimed invention; provide a convincing line of reasoning taught by the prior art or provided by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning/rationale should be taught by applied art or be provided by examiner and form a convincing line of reasoning as to why the artisan would have found the claimed invention obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection compliance — identify claim/statute and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 103 rejection is made, determine whether all 35 USC 103 rejection(s) in the Office action are in compliance (Yes/No). Compliance requires properly identifying the claim(s), the statute (including subparagraphs) and being supported by sufficient evidence to support the conclusion of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statutory compliance standard and scenarios for guidance. If noncompliant, proceed to identify claims and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify claims linked to noncompliant 103 rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: List each claim discussed individually as a basis for noncompliance for a 103 rejection; include dependent claims inheriting noncompliance; indicate whether root of noncompliance originates in independent or dependent claims or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain in the Explanation of Noncompliance section the basis for each listed claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for alternate compliant prior art rejection when 103 noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims with a noncompliant 103 rejection, determine whether another compliant prior art rejection (either under 102 or 103) was applied to those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every claim listed as noncompliant under 103 also has another compliant prior art rejection, answer Yes; otherwise No. Indicate whether the compliant prior art rejection(s) was applied under 102 and/or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 103 noncompliance reason — failure to properly identify claims/statute
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute/subparagraph for the 103 rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claim listing or statute identification is incorrect; do not use if the issue is lack of evidentiary support (use the insufficient evidence box).

rubrics_metrics.name: 103 noncompliance reason — disclosure not prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure(s) relied upon in the 103 rejection does not qualify as prior art under any statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure could be prior art but not under the subparagraph applied, use the failure-to-identify-statute box instead. Provide factual explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 103 noncompliance reason — failure to establish prima facie case of obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection fails to provide sufficient evidence to establish a prima facie case of obviousness (insufficient findings of fact, missing limitation mappings, unsupported combinations, or lack of articulated rationale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If checked, identify the basis for lack of sufficient evidence by selecting subitems (e.g., findings of fact not properly articulated/evidenced; missing mapping; mapping insufficient; combination rationale absent). Provide specific examples and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 103 noncompliance subcriterion — findings of fact not properly articulated/evidenced
rubrics_metrics.description: For 103 noncompliance when findings of fact are not properly articulated/evidenced (e.g., missing limitation), determine whether the rejection correlated the missing element to the primary reference, a secondary reference, or Official Notice; check whether there was no citation/mapping or mapping is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 4(c)(i) is checked, also check whether correlation was to primary reference, secondary reference, or Official Notice and whether there was no citation/mapping or the mapping was insufficient. Give concrete examples showing missing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 103 rejection comments / best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional comments providing suggestions, feedback, or best practices for the examiner concerning 103 rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewer suggests a compliant prior art rejection for TC consideration, include details here. Comments should be actionable and not substitute the statutory compliance write-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search/Prior Art — search strategy and documentation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the examiner's search covered the inventive concept and whether search documentation (search printout, search notes) is present documenting search strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a similarity search was attempted but failed, indicate Yes. If search documentation is absent or for a different application, indicate No and explain in comments. Reviewer may perform their own search and must document full search history if so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search/Prior Art characteristics — inventive concept coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic: The search includes the inventive concept (assume claims are directed to the invention; if search misses claimed invention, do not check).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanation in comment box if the search is missing the claimed invention; check when search appropriately targets inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search/Prior Art characteristics — consultation with experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic: Evidence present of consultation with experts during the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when documentation indicates examiner consulted subject matter experts as part of the search process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search/Prior Art characteristics — prior art cited pertinent to significant unclaimed features
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic: Prior art was cited on the record which was pertinent to significant unclaimed features of the disclosed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check this if examiner cited additional art not applied to the claims but relevant to unclaimed aspects; optionally include explanation of relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search/Prior Art characteristics — brief description for relevant prior art cited but not applied
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic: A brief description was provided for relevant prior art cited but not applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when examiner cites art not applied to claims and also explains relevance in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search/Prior Art characteristics — search printout includes designation of result sets reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic: The search printout includes designations of which result sets were reviewed (MPEP 719.05(II)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check when search output shows which results were actually reviewed; aids reproducibility and quality assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-performed search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reviewer performed a search, the reviewer should document whether they performed a search and provide a complete history of all search parameters (databases searched, search logic for each database, CPC/keyword/inventor/assignee/NPL/forward/backwards/sequence, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer’s independent search must be fully documented; merely accessing prosecution-record art via a tool without a search does not count as a Reviewer Search.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(f) three-prong analysis for invocation
rubrics_metrics.description: As the reviewer, perform the three-prong analysis (MPEP 2181(I)) to determine whether any claim limitations invoke 112(f) (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base this on the reviewer's independent application of the three-prong test; identify specific limitations invoking 112(f) in comments if not documented by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorded statements regarding 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the prosecution record includes any statements regarding the examiner’s determination about 112(f) being invoked or not invoked (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reviewer finds invocation that is not reflected in the record, identify those limitations in the comment box. If many limitations are present, the reviewer may list a representative subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of 112(f) presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the 112(f) presumptions were documented in the record (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document whether examiner noted presumptions and whether any limitations were identified as overcoming the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness of 112(f) statements on record
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether all statements made on the record regarding 112(f) invocation (or lack thereof) are correct (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This question checks legal correctness of recorded statements; if No, include explanation in the 112(f) comment box.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(f) analysis comments and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional suggestions or feedback to the examiner regarding 112(f) analysis, documentation, or best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include actionable guidance; this is optional except where earlier questions require specific commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction/election requirement present and proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether a requirement for restriction/election is present in the Office action and whether the requirement for restriction/election was proper (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If improper, indicate specific defects: burden not met; does not meet distinctness/independent requirements; wrong practice (e.g., 371 vs US); inventions should have been subjected to election by original presentation. Provide supporting explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of rationale for restriction/election
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a sufficient rationale was provided in support of a restriction/election requirement (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If No, document what rationale is missing or inadequate in the comment box and suggest corrective practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action typographical/grammatical quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the Office action is generally free from typographical/grammatical errors (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer No if situations occur such as: rejection addresses a specific claim in the body but that claim not listed in the statement; a cancelled claim is included in the statement of rejection; AIA 103 references 'time the invention was made' instead of effective filing; substantive copy/paste errors; typographical errors in reference numbers or inventor names; references mentioned in body but not included in statement of rejection, etc. Provide examples in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action tone — professional and courteous
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the Office action was written in a tone which is professional and courteous (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note unprofessional language or personalization issues in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of duplicative rejections for compact prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether duplicative rejections were used only for compact prosecution and were not unnecessary (Yes/No/NA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If duplicative rejections are present, document why they were appropriate for compact prosecution or why they were unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other quality issues — capture issues not described elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture other issues not described in other sections and indicate whether they require attention from the Technology Center (No; Yes (Attention Needed); Yes (Not Attention Needed)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples for 'Yes (Not Attention Needed)' include minor form or miscellaneous issues observed which do not require correction before issuance. Use 'Yes (Attention Needed)' for allowances with substantive errors that the TC should correct before issuance. List specific issues in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed back-up prior art rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the reviewer proposes any back-up prior art rejection(s) for claims that already have a compliant prior art rejection (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in rare situations where a back-up rejection provides meaningful protection against easily-invoked exceptions; the back-up must be a complete rejection fully explained. Do not use to propose general additional rejections; if no compliant prior art rejection exists, raise as an omitted rejection instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accolade eligibility for Search/Prior Art, 112(f), Restriction, Other Quality Issues, Finality
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple sections there is the possibility to indicate an accolade (Yes/No) if the work meets established criteria; when Yes, the reviewer must complete a sentence per current accolade procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult current accolade procedures and guidance documents before indicating Yes; appropriate wording must be used for accolade letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Office action (proper finality/prosecution closed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office action is Final, determine whether the finality of the Office action was proper (prosecution actually closed) (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If No, indicate reasons (e.g., new grounds not necessitated by amendment; first action final after RCE with advisory action issues; IDS submitted with incorrect fee/statement handling) and provide comments.
